name: Treating "high blood" by how you feel
what_people_do: Older Black women describe "high blood" or "high-pertension" as something felt in the blood and nerves, and manage medication by those symptoms.
why_they_say_it_works: The illness is understood through symptoms and life stress rather than a number on a cuff.

documented_by.source: Heurtin-Roberts S 1993, Soc Sci Med, PMID 8356478
documented_by.quote_or_summary: 60 older African American women in New Orleans: "high-pertension" is a chronic folk illness involving blood and "nerves", and a way of adapting to life.

documented_by.source: Heurtin-Roberts S, Reisin E 1992, Am J Hypertens, PMID 1457078
documented_by.quote_or_summary: 60 black hypertensive women at Charity Hospital: 53% held a "high blood" or "high-pertension" model; the model was significantly related to compliance with treatment (P<0.01 to 0.001) and compliance to blood pressure control (P=0.05).

evidence.finding: Illness model related to compliance, and compliance to BP control; small clinic sample.

source.name: Heurtin-Roberts S, Reisin E 1992, Am J Hypertens, PMID 1457078

harm_note: Adjusting tablets by symptoms rather than by readings is unsafe for a condition that is often silent.
gaps: 1992 and 1993, one city; current prevalence unknown.
